## Outsourced compliance officer

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/outsourced-compliance-officer.html

An outsourced AML compliance officer, or MLRO, for businesses FINTRAC regulates. US$1,500 per 10 hours, scaled as you grow.

**Fee:** US$1,500 (per 10 hours · scalable). How your hours are used each month is set out in your written scope.

**Included:**
- All AML and compliance obligations under your program
- Second-line review of customer onboarding
- Advice on cases, products and regulatory questions
- Regulatory reporting: STR, EFTR, LVCTR, LCTR and others
- Policy and procedure maintenance
- Business risk assessment
- Client risk assessments
- Hours that scale as your business grows

### What an outsourced compliance officer does

Under the PCMLTFA, a business that FINTRAC regulates must appoint a compliance officer who is responsible for implementing its compliance program. FINTRAC's guidance says that person needs the authority and the access to resources to do the job. For a larger business, FINTRAC's guidance suggests someone from a senior level with direct access to senior management and the board.

An outsourced compliance officer fills that role, or supports the person who holds it, from outside the business. FINTRAC's guidance doesn't specifically address external appointments, so we document the compliance officer's authority, access to senior management and sign-off responsibilities in writing. The arrangement is common for money services businesses, virtual currency dealers, payment companies and foreign businesses entering Canada, which need experienced compliance judgment without a full-time senior hire.

The work is ongoing. Customers are onboarded every day, transactions need watching, reports have deadlines measured in days, and the rules and your business both change. We do that work with your team, inside your systems.

### What's included

The scope covers your AML and compliance obligations as a whole. This is the work most often involved.

### Second-line customer onboarding review

Your front line collects customer information. As the second line, we review it: how identity was verified, beneficial ownership, politically exposed person and head of international organization determinations, third-party determinations, sanctions and listed person screening results, and the customer's risk rating. We approve or escalate files, apply enhanced measures where the risk is high, and sample completed files to check that the process holds up.

### Advisory

Questions don't wait for a review cycle. A new product, a new market, a new agent, a payment partner's due diligence questionnaire, a bank asking about your program, or a letter from FINTRAC. We give you a clear answer, explain the reasoning, and record the decision so you can show it later.

### Regulatory reporting

We prepare and file the reports your business has to make to FINTRAC, including suspicious transaction reports, electronic funds transfer reports, large virtual currency transaction reports, large cash transaction reports and listed person or entity property reports. Each one has its own threshold and deadline:

| Report | When it applies | Deadline |

| Suspicious transaction report (STR) | Reasonable grounds to suspect a transaction is related to money laundering, terrorist financing or, since August 19, 2024, sanctions evasion. No minimum amount. | As soon as practicable |

| Large cash transaction report (LCTR) | Cash of $10,000 or more, in one transaction or in two or more that the 24-hour rule requires you to add together. | 15 calendar days |

| Electronic funds transfer report (EFTR) | International electronic funds transfers of $10,000 or more, in one transfer or in two or more that the 24-hour rule requires you to add together. | 5 working days |

| Large virtual currency transaction report (LVCTR) | Virtual currency worth $10,000 or more, in one transaction or in two or more that the 24-hour rule requires you to add together. | 5 working days |

| Listed person or entity property report | Property you know or believe is owned or controlled by a terrorist group or a listed person or entity. Since October 1, 2025, this includes persons listed under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Sergei Magnitsky Law. Called the terrorist property report until March 2, 2025. You must also disclose the property to the RCMP and CSIS without delay. | Immediately |

Amounts are in Canadian dollars. Under FINTRAC's 24-hour rule, two or more transactions that total $10,000 or more within a static 24-hour window are reported together when you know they were conducted by or on behalf of the same person or entity, or are for the same beneficiary.

### Policy maintenance

Your compliance policies and procedures have to be kept up to date. We update them when the regulations change, when FINTRAC publishes new guidance, and when your business launches something new, and we keep a record of what changed and why.

### Business risk assessment

Your program rests on a documented assessment of your money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion risks: your clients and business relationships, your products, services and delivery channels, where you operate, and new technologies. We write it, keep it current and check that your controls follow from it.

### Client risk assessments

Every client gets a risk rating that drives how closely you monitor them. We set the methodology, review ratings and apply enhanced measures to high-risk clients.

### How the engagement runs

- **Consultation.** Your business, your customers, your volumes and what you already have in place.

- **Written scope.** What we'll do, how many hours to start with, and how we'll report the time to you.

- **Set-up.** Access to the systems we need, such as your onboarding and screening tools and your FINTRAC reporting account, and a handover of open items.

- **Ongoing work.** Onboarding reviews, reporting, advice and maintenance, with regular check-ins with your management.

- **Scaling.** As volumes grow, add blocks of hours, or hand the work to an in-house compliance officer we help you hire and train.

### How many hours you might need

It depends on how many customers you onboard, how many alerts and reports you generate, how many products and markets you serve, and whether you deal in cash or virtual currency. A business preparing to launch needs far fewer hours than one onboarding hundreds of customers a month.

We estimate a starting number of hours with you in the consultation, then adjust once your volumes are clear. Hours are bought in blocks of 10, so the cost follows your workload.

### Your responsibilities, and ours

Your business remains the reporting entity even when we do the work, and your senior management stays accountable for the program. We document decisions, send escalations to the right people and keep you informed of what was done in your name.

- You provide access, information and timely decisions.

- We carry out the agreed work, flag risks early and keep records you can show an examiner.

- We agree in writing who signs off on what, including reports and policy changes.

### MLRO, compliance officer or CCO?

The titles differ by country. In the UK and Europe the role is usually called the MLRO, or money laundering reporting officer. Canada's PCMLTFA framework uses "compliance officer", and many firms use "chief compliance officer" too. If you're entering Canada from abroad and looking for an MLRO, the Canadian compliance officer is the equivalent role, with Canada's own reports, thresholds and deadlines.

### Questions

**Can a business outsource its compliance officer in Canada?** Many businesses use an outside compliance officer, or outside support for the person they appoint. FINTRAC's guidance doesn't specifically address external appointments. Your business stays responsible for its obligations, and the compliance officer needs the authority and access to senior management to do the job, so we set out authority, access and sign-off in writing.

**What does an outsourced compliance officer cost?** US$1,500 for each block of 10 hours. You choose how many blocks you need, and you can add more as your business grows.

**What is an MLRO in Canada?** MLRO means money laundering reporting officer, a title used mainly in the UK and Europe. The Canadian equivalent under the PCMLTFA is the compliance officer.

**Which FINTRAC reports do you handle?** Suspicious transaction reports, electronic funds transfer reports, large virtual currency transaction reports, large cash transaction reports, and listed person or entity property reports, whichever apply to your business.

**Do you work with foreign money services businesses?** Yes. We work with businesses based outside Canada that serve people in Canada.

**Can we start small?** Yes. Start with the hours you need now, and add blocks of 10 hours when your volumes grow.

**Is a fractional compliance officer the same as an outsourced one?** In practice, yes. "Fractional" usually means a part-time compliance officer from outside your business who is paid for the hours used. Our service works that way: you buy blocks of 10 hours for US$1,500 and add more as your volumes grow.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Compliance program requirements](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/compliance-conformite/Guide4/4-eng); [Reporting suspicious transactions](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/str-dod/str-dod-eng); [Reporting suspected sanctions evasion](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/sanctions/sanctions-eng); [Reporting listed person or entity property](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/Guide5/5-eng); [Reporting electronic funds transfers](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/eft-dt/eft-dt-eng); [Reporting large virtual currency transactions](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/lvctr/lvctr-eng); [Reporting large cash transactions](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/lctr-doie/lctr-doie-eng); [The 24-hour rule](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/24hour/1-eng). Checked 11 October 2026.

## MSB registration

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration.html

For money services businesses, foreign MSBs and virtual currency dealers. Fixed fee US$3,500.

**Fee:** US$3,500 (fixed fee · one time). Covers your registration. Compliance program documents are a separate fixed fee of US$3,500.

**Included:**
- Assessment of which of your activities are money services
- Registration information gathered and checked with you
- Ownership, corporate and criminal record check requirements coordinated, including certified translations
- Submission, and answers to FINTRAC's follow-up questions
- Foreign MSB requirements, including your representative for service in Canada
- Coordination with your compliance program

### Who has to register

A business with a place of business in Canada must register with FINTRAC before it operates as a money services business, for example by dealing in foreign exchange, remitting or transmitting funds, or dealing in virtual currency. Registering or being licensed with a province doesn't replace FINTRAC registration. Whether your own activities are covered depends on how your business works, which is the first thing we confirm with you.

An MSB that holds funds for its users or transfers funds at their request may also need to register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act. We cover that in [RPAA registration](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration.html).

Our guide on [how to register an MSB in Canada](https://amlcanada.ca/how-to-register-msb-canada.html) lists every money service and walks through each step of the application.

### Foreign MSB registration

A foreign MSB has no place of business in Canada but directs and provides money services to people or entities in Canada. It registers with FINTRAC before it starts and names a representative for service who resides in Canada; our [foreign MSB guide](https://amlcanada.ca/foreign-msb-registration-canada.html) covers the details.

### What the application involves

FINTRAC asks for details of the business, its owners, senior management and compliance officer, its bank accounts, locations and agents, and its expected transaction volumes, with documents showing who owns and controls it. Criminal record checks are needed for the chief executive officer, the president, the directors and anyone who owns or controls 20% or more. A document that isn't in English or French needs a translation attested by a certified translator (PCMLTFA s.11.12(1.1)).

If FINTRAC asks for clarification, the answer is due within 30 days of the request, or FINTRAC can deny the application (PCMLTFA s.11.14). Registered businesses face the same 30-day limit, with revocation as the consequence (s.11.17).

### How registration works with us

- **Assessment.** Which of your services are money services, whether you're an MSB or a foreign MSB, and what follows from that.

- **Preparation.** A checklist of everything FINTRAC needs, and help gathering and checking it. Criminal record checks from several countries often take longest, so we start them first.

- **Submission.** Your registration, submitted to FINTRAC with your approval.

- **Follow-up.** Answers to FINTRAC's questions, within its deadlines, until your registration is decided.

- **Compliance program.** Prepared at the same time as your registration, so you can operate once you're registered.

### How long registration takes

FINTRAC says most complete applications are processed within three months. In our experience it has ranged from about 1 week to 7 months. The main factors are how complete and consistent the application is, how quickly criminal record checks arrive, and FINTRAC's workload at the time.

### After you register

Registration is valid for two years and has to be renewed before it expires. Changes to your registration information must be reported to FINTRAC within 30 days.

After registration, an MSB also needs a compliance program, client identification, record keeping and reporting to FINTRAC. Since October 1, 2025, an MSB must also check that its agents and mandataries are eligible, including by reviewing criminal record checks, before engaging them.

### Virtual currency dealers

Dealing in virtual currency is a money service, so crypto exchanges and dealers register with FINTRAC as MSBs, including foreign ones that serve people in Canada. Registered dealers also report virtual currency transactions of $10,000 or more within five working days. Provincial securities rules can also apply to some crypto trading platforms; we'll tell you if that's something you need separate advice on.

### Questions

**How much does MSB registration cost?** FINTRAC doesn't charge a registration fee. Our fee to prepare and support your registration is a fixed US$3,500.

**How long does FINTRAC registration take?** FINTRAC says most complete applications are processed within three months. In our experience it has ranged from about 1 week to 7 months, depending mostly on how complete the application is, how quickly criminal record checks arrive, and FINTRAC's workload.

**Can a company outside Canada register as an MSB?** Yes. A foreign business that directs and provides money services to people in Canada registers as a foreign MSB and must name a representative for service who resides in Canada.

**Do I need a compliance program before I register?** You need one to operate. FINTRAC asks for your compliance officer when you register, and your obligations start as soon as you begin. We prepare your program at the same time as your registration. Program documents are a separate fixed fee of US$3,500.

**How often do I renew?** Every two years. Changes to your registration information have to be reported within 30 days.

**Do crypto businesses register with FINTRAC?** Yes. Dealing in virtual currency is a money service, so crypto dealers and exchanges register as MSBs.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Money services businesses](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/msb-eng); [Register your MSB or FMSB](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng); [Update, renew or cancel your registration](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/respond-eng); [Reporting large virtual currency transactions](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/lvctr/lvctr-eng); [PCMLTFA, sections 11.1 to 11.17](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/P-24.501/); [Bank of Canada, Retail payments](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/regulatory-oversight/retail-payments/). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Compliance programs

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/compliance-programs.html

FINTRAC and PCMLTFA compliance program documents for the businesses FINTRAC regulates. Fixed fee US$3,500.

**Fee:** US$3,500 (fixed fee · program documents). Keeping the program current afterwards can be covered by outsourced compliance officer hours.

**Included:**
- AML/ATF Compliance Policy
- KYC and Customer Due Diligence Procedure
- Ongoing Monitoring Procedure
- Business-Wide Risk Assessment
- Sanctions and Watchlist Screening Policy and Procedure
- Ministerial Directive Compliance Policy
- Travel Rule Policy and Procedure
- Applicable FINTRAC Reporting Procedures
- Procedural Registers
- Records Retention Policy
- Staff AML Training Policy
- Compliance Testing and Effectiveness Review Plan
- Risk Appetite Policy
- Fraud Risk Management Policy

### The 14 documents you receive

Your fixed fee covers a complete set of PCMLTFA compliance program documents for your business:

- AML/ATF Compliance Policy

- KYC and Customer Due Diligence Procedure

- Ongoing Monitoring Procedure

- Business-Wide Risk Assessment

- Sanctions and Watchlist Screening Policy and Procedure

- Ministerial Directive Compliance Policy

- Travel Rule Policy and Procedure

- Applicable FINTRAC Reporting Procedures

- Procedural Registers

- Records Retention Policy

- Staff AML Training Policy

- Compliance Testing and Effectiveness Review Plan

- Risk Appetite Policy

- Fraud Risk Management Policy

Together they cover the policies, procedures, risk assessment, training and review planning behind the five required parts of a FINTRAC compliance program, plus your risk appetite and fraud risk management.

### The five parts of a compliance program

FINTRAC's guidance sets out five required elements:

- **A compliance officer**, appointed to be responsible for implementing the program.

- **Written policies and procedures**, kept up to date and, for an entity, approved by a senior officer.

- **A risk assessment** of the business's money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion risks, documented.

- **A written, ongoing compliance training program**, with a plan for delivering it, if you have employees, agents or others authorized to act for you.

- **A review of effectiveness** of the policies and procedures, risk assessment and training program, at least every two years.

### What your policies and procedures cover

- knowing your client: verifying identity, beneficial ownership, and politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations;

- third-party determinations and business relationships;

- ongoing monitoring, and the enhanced measures you apply to high-risk clients;

- sanctions and listed person screening;

- reporting to FINTRAC, including suspicious transactions, and the 24-hour rule;

- record keeping;

- ministerial directives, and how you'll apply new ones;

- travel rule information for funds and virtual currency transfers, where it applies.

The exact list depends on the kind of business you are and the services you offer, which is why we start with how you operate.

### Your risk assessment

The rest of your program depends on the risk assessment. It looks at your money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion risks: your clients and business relationships, your products, services and delivery channels, the places you operate in and deal with, new developments and technologies, and the risks for your sector set out in Canada's latest National Risk Assessment of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing. Higher-risk clients and products get closer controls.

### If your bank or payment partner has asked for your program

Banks and payment partners usually want to see that your program exists, fits your business, has a named compliance officer, and is followed day to day. If you've been asked and don't have one, or aren't sure yours will stand up, book a consultation. We'll tell you what's missing and how quickly it can be put right.

### Keeping it current

A program written once and left on a shelf goes out of date as your business and the rules change. We can keep it current through outsourced compliance officer hours, and test it in your two-year effectiveness review.

### Questions

**What does an AML compliance program include in Canada?** Five parts: a compliance officer, written policies and procedures, a risk assessment, an ongoing training program and plan if you have employees, agents or others acting for you, and an effectiveness review at least every two years.

**How much does a compliance program cost?** A fixed US$3,500 for 14 PCMLTFA compliance program documents, from the AML/ATF Compliance Policy to the Fraud Risk Management Policy.

**Do you use templates?** We use a consistent structure, and the content is written for your products, customers and team. A program that doesn't describe how your business works won't hold up in an examination.

**Does the fee include the effectiveness review?** No. The program includes a plan for your review. The review itself is a separate, scoped piece of work.

**Can you keep the program up to date afterwards?** Yes, through outsourced compliance officer hours at US$1,500 per 10 hours.

**Our bank has asked for our AML program. What now?** Book a consultation. We'll look at what you have, tell you what's missing and agree a written scope to close the gaps.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Compliance program requirements](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/compliance-conformite/Guide4/4-eng); [Changes to the PCMLTFA and regulations](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/businesses-entreprises/changes-changements-eng); [Money services businesses](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/msb-eng); [The 24-hour rule](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/transaction-operation/24hour/1-eng). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Canadian business address

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/canadian-address.html

A Canadian business address for your setup, banking and partners, for foreign MSBs and companies entering Canada. US$200 per month.

**Fee:** US$200 (per month). Often combined with MSB registration and an outsourced compliance officer.

**Included:**
- A Canadian business address
- For your setup, banking and partners
- Scope, including mail handling, confirmed in writing
- Checked against your FINTRAC registration before you use it

### Why a Canadian address helps

Canadian banks, payment partners and customers often look for a Canadian presence, and a Canadian business address gives your setup a stable base. For a Canadian-based MSB, FINTRAC registration asks for every location you operate from.

### How the address fits your FINTRAC registration

A foreign MSB registers with FINTRAC through a representative for service: a person who resides in Canada and accepts FINTRAC's notices on the business's behalf. That's a separate requirement from your business address.

If you're a foreign MSB, a physical location in Canada can change your status to a domestic MSB. We'll confirm how the address fits your registration before you use it.

### How it works

- **Consultation.** Your plans for Canada and how you'll use the address.

- **Written scope.** What's included, including mail handling.

- **Registration check.** How the address fits your FINTRAC registration, if you have one or are applying.

- **Start.** Your address is ready to use with your banks and partners.

- **Monthly.** US$200 per month while you use it.

### Questions

**How much is a Canadian business address?** US$200 per month.

**Can I use the address on my FINTRAC registration?** It depends on how you're registered. A foreign MSB registers with a representative for service who resides in Canada, and a physical location in Canada can change a foreign MSB into a domestic MSB. We confirm how the address fits your registration before you use it.

**Is the address my representative for service?** No. A foreign MSB's representative for service is a person who resides in Canada, which is a separate requirement. Ask us about it in your consultation.

**What happens to mail sent to the address?** How mail is handled is set out in your written scope.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Register your MSB or FMSB](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng); [Money services businesses](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/msb-eng). Checked 11 October 2026.

## MSB for sale

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/msb-for-sale.html

Acquire a Canadian company already registered with FINTRAC as a money services business. From €28,000.

**Fee:** €28,000 (starting price · acquisition). Compliance program, compliance officer and Canadian address are available alongside, at their own fees.

**Included:**
- A Canadian company registered with FINTRAC as an MSB
- Company records and registration history reviewed with you
- Eligibility of the new owners and directors checked
- Support through the change of ownership
- Updates to FINTRAC within 30 days, including new owners and directors
- Guidance on what the new owners need to provide

### How buying a registered MSB works

- **Consultation.** Your plans: the services you'll offer, your customers and your timeline.

- **Matching.** A company registered for the money services you need.

- **Due diligence.** Corporate records, registration status and history, and the eligibility of the new owners and directors, reviewed before you commit.

- **Bank of Canada.** If the company is also registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act, re-registration before the purchase closes.

- **Change of ownership.** The transfer of the company's shares to you.

- **FINTRAC updates.** Changes to the registration information, such as owners, directors and compliance officer, reported within 30 days.

### What to check before you buy

- that the registration is active and covers the services you plan to offer;

- when the registration is next due for renewal;

- the company's corporate records, ownership history and any past compliance issues;

- that the new owners and directors are eligible. Under PCMLTFA s.11.11, a business can't be registered if, for example, a director, the chief executive officer, the president or a 20% owner has certain criminal convictions, or if a FINTRAC penalty remains unpaid;

- that the chief executive officer, the president, the directors and anyone owning or controlling 20% or more can provide criminal record checks, with a certified translation for any that aren't in English or French;

- whether the company is also registered with the Bank of Canada as a payment service provider;

- whether provincial requirements apply where you'll operate. Quebec, for example, licenses money services businesses separately.

Our guide to [buying an MSB in Canada](https://amlcanada.ca/buying-an-msb-canada.html) has the full due-diligence checklist.

### If the company is also registered with the Bank of Canada

Some MSBs are also registered with the Bank of Canada as payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Buying control of such a company is an acquisition of control, so the company must apply again and be re-registered by the Bank before the purchase closes (RPAA s.24). The changes are then reported to FINTRAC within 30 days.

### After the purchase

The obligations come with the company. The business needs a compliance officer and a compliance program that reflect its new owners and services, and it must report to FINTRAC, keep records and renew its registration every two years. FINTRAC registration doesn't guarantee a bank account or payment partners, which make their own decisions.

### Buying an MSB or registering a new one

| | Register a new MSB | Buy a registered MSB |

| Our fee | US$3,500, fixed | From €28,000 |

| Starting point | A new or existing company of yours | A company already registered |

| Main wait | Preparing the application and FINTRAC's review | Due diligence, the change of ownership and any Bank of Canada re-registration |

| Afterwards | The same obligations: compliance program, reporting, record keeping and renewal |

### Questions

**How much does a registered MSB cost?** Acquisitions start from €28,000. The price depends on the company, the services it's registered for and its history.

**Does the FINTRAC registration stay with the company?** The registration belongs to the registered business, so the purchase is of the company's shares; a new entity would need its own registration. After the purchase, FINTRAC must be told about changes to the registration information, such as new owners and directors, within 30 days.

**Do the new owners need criminal record checks?** FINTRAC asks for criminal record checks for the chief executive officer, the president, the directors and anyone owning or controlling 20% or more of the business. Any check that isn't in English or French needs a translation attested by a certified translator.

**What if the company is registered with the Bank of Canada too?** Then it must apply again and be re-registered by the Bank before the purchase closes. We check this during due diligence.

**Does it come with a bank account?** FINTRAC registration doesn't guarantee banking or payment partners. We discuss what each company has in place before you commit.

**Can a buyer outside Canada acquire an MSB?** Yes. Foreign buyers can acquire a registered Canadian company, subject to the same FINTRAC requirements.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Register your MSB or FMSB](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng); [Update, renew or cancel your registration](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/respond-eng); [Money services businesses](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/msb-eng); [PCMLTFA, section 11.11](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/P-24.501/); [Bank of Canada, Acquisitions of control and prescribed changes](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2024/08/acquisitions-of-control-and-prescribed-changes/). Checked 11 October 2026.

## RPAA registration

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration.html

Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration for payment service providers. Fixed fee US$3,500, plus the Bank's application fee.

**Fee:** US$3,500 (fixed fee · plus the Bank of Canada application fee). The Bank's application fee is non-refundable and paid to the Bank. It was CA$2,500 when introduced in November 2024 and is indexed to inflation each January under the Retail Payment Activities Regulations; we confirm the current amount before you apply. RPAA compliance program documents are a separate fixed fee of US$3,500.

**Included:**
- Assessment of whether the RPAA applies to your activities
- Registration application prepared with you
- Your payment activities, agents, mandataries and third parties described
- Support through the Bank's questions and any national security review
- Coordination with your FINTRAC registration, where you need both

### Does the RPAA apply to you?

The Act covers businesses that perform payment functions for end users as a service or business activity, such as holding accounts or funds for end users, initiating, authorizing or transmitting electronic funds transfers, and providing clearing or settlement services. A PSP with a place of business in Canada is covered. A PSP outside Canada is covered when it directs retail payment activities at people or entities in Canada and performs them for end users in Canada (RPAA s.5).

Banks and some other institutions are excluded, and some activities fall outside the Act, so we confirm where you stand before preparing anything. Our [RPAA guide](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration-guide.html) explains the Act in more detail.

### What it costs

Our fee is a fixed US$3,500. The Bank's one-time, non-refundable application fee was CA$2,500 when it was introduced in November 2024 and is indexed to inflation each January, so we confirm the current amount before you apply.

The Bank also plans to charge registered PSPs annual assessment fees to recover its supervision costs. It isn't charging them yet and will start once the cost-recovery regulations are finalized.

### How we handle your application

- **Assessment.** Which of your activities are retail payment activities, and whether you need FINTRAC registration as well.

- **Preparation.** Your business, ownership, payment activities, agents, mandataries and third-party providers, gathered and checked.

- **Application.** Submitted to the Bank of Canada, with the application fee.

- **Review.** The Bank shares applications with the Department of Finance and FINTRAC, and the Minister of Finance can order a national security review. We help you answer questions along the way.

- **Decision.** Once registered, your business is listed in the Bank's public registry of PSPs.

In our experience the process often takes 2 to 8 months, though that isn't guaranteed. A new PSP can't start retail payment activities until the Bank registers it, so we plan the timeline with you from the start.

### After registration

Registered PSPs need a risk management and incident response framework and, if they hold end-user funds, a safeguarding framework. They also report incidents, changes and an annual report to the Bank. Our [RPAA compliance program](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-compliance-program.html) sets these up for a fixed US$3,500.

### RPAA and FINTRAC: do you need both?

Often, yes. A payment business that remits or transmits funds usually needs FINTRAC registration as an MSB as well. The Bank's regime deals with operational risk and the safety of users' funds, and FINTRAC's with money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion. We can prepare both registrations together.

### Questions

**How much does RPAA registration cost?** Our fee is a fixed US$3,500. The Bank of Canada also charges a one-time, non-refundable application fee, which was CA$2,500 when introduced in November 2024 and is indexed to inflation each January. We confirm the current amount before you apply.

**Is the Bank of Canada fee included in your price?** No. The application fee is paid directly to the Bank and isn't part of our US$3,500.

**Do foreign payment service providers have to register?** Yes, if they direct retail payment activities at people or entities in Canada and perform them for end users in Canada.

**Do I also need to register with FINTRAC?** Often. If you also provide money services, such as remitting or transmitting funds, you need FINTRAC registration as an MSB too.

**How long does RPAA registration take?** In our experience it often takes 2 to 8 months, including any national security review. That isn't guaranteed, and a new PSP can't start retail payment activities until it's registered.

**What happens after registration?** You need risk management, incident response and, if you hold end-user funds, safeguarding frameworks, plus incident notices, change notices and annual reports. Our RPAA compliance program covers these.

Sources: [Bank of Canada, Retail payments](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/regulatory-oversight/retail-payments/); [Supervisory framework](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/regulatory-oversight/retail-payments/supervisory-framework/); [Frequently asked questions about retail payments supervision](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/08/frequently-asked-questions-about-retail-payments-supervision/); [Registration application fee](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2024/10/registration-application-fee/); [Criteria for registering PSPs](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/06/criteria-for-registering-payment-service-providers/); [Registry of payment service providers](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/regulatory-oversight/retail-payments/psp-registry/). Checked 11 October 2026.

## RPAA compliance program

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-compliance-program.html

Risk management, incident response and safeguarding frameworks for payment service providers. Fixed fee US$3,500.

**Fee:** US$3,500 (fixed fee · program documents). Ongoing support, such as preparing your annual report, can be covered by outsourced compliance officer hours.

**Included:**
- Senior officer and governance
- Risk framework and registers
- Incident response
- Third parties and agents
- Safeguarding
- Cyber, IT and continuity
- Annual report and change notices

### Senior officer and governance

Clear roles and responsibilities, with a senior officer accountable for the frameworks, and enough resources to run them. We set out who owns each framework, how it's approved and reviewed, and how issues reach senior management.

### Risk framework and registers

The Bank expects PSPs to identify their operational risks, protect against them, detect problems, and respond and recover, with periodic review and testing. We build your risk framework and the registers behind it: the risks in your payment activities, the controls that address them and who is responsible.

### Incident response

When something goes wrong, your team needs to know what to do. The framework covers how incidents are identified, escalated, contained and recovered from. When you determine that an incident has a material impact, you notify the Bank and any affected end users, PSPs and clearing houses without delay, and no later than 48 hours after that determination.

### Third parties and agents

Many PSPs depend on processors, banks, cloud providers and others, and some act through agents or mandataries. The framework covers how you assess and manage the risks they bring. Foreign PSPs also identify the agents or mandataries acting for them in Canada.

### Safeguarding end-user funds

If you hold end-user funds, you must safeguard them, either in a trust account, or in a segregated account protected by insurance or a guarantee. Your written safeguarding framework explains how end users get timely access to their funds and how funds would be paid out if your business became insolvent.

### Cyber, IT and continuity

Protecting the integrity, confidentiality and availability of your systems and data, detecting cyber threats, and keeping payments running, or restoring them quickly, when systems or providers fail.

### Annual report and change notices

PSPs file an annual report with the Bank no later than March 31 of the following year. The Bank lists its contents as up-to-date information on risk management and incident response, safeguarding of end-user funds where that applies, and certain financial and activity metrics.

Changes to registration information are generally notified within 30 days after they happen, and certain changes at least 30 or 60 days before they take effect (Retail Payment Activities Regulations, ss.35 and 36). A significant change or new activity needs notice at least five business days before. An acquisition of control needs a new application, approved by the Bank before the acquisition closes (RPAA s.24). The framework sets out how you track, prepare and approve each of these.

### Questions

**What does the RPAA require from payment service providers?** Risk management and incident response frameworks, safeguarding of end-user funds where you hold them, incident notices within 48 hours of determining an incident is material, change notices, and an annual report by March 31.

**How much does an RPAA compliance program cost?** A fixed US$3,500 for the program documents covering all seven areas.

**Is this the same as our FINTRAC AML program?** No. The RPAA program covers operational risk and safeguarding under the Bank of Canada. A FINTRAC compliance program covers money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion. Many payment businesses need both.

**Do you help us put the frameworks in place?** Yes. We write them around how you operate and walk your team through them. Ongoing support can be covered by outsourced compliance officer hours.

Sources: [Bank of Canada, Supervisory framework](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/regulatory-oversight/retail-payments/supervisory-framework/); [Retail payments](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/regulatory-oversight/retail-payments/); [Reminder: PSP reporting obligations under the RPAA](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/06/reminder-psp-reporting-obligations-under-rpaa/); [Acquisitions of control and prescribed changes](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2024/08/acquisitions-of-control-and-prescribed-changes/); [Retail Payment Activities Regulations](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2023-229/). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Effectiveness reviews

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/effectiveness-reviews.html

The two-year effectiveness review FINTRAC requires, and preparation for a FINTRAC examination.

**Fee:** Scoped (quoted after your consultation). Depends on your size, products and the number of files to test.

**Included:**
- A scoped review, agreed in writing
- Testing of what happens against what's written
- Written findings and recommendations, in order of priority
- Help preparing records and your team for an examination

### How often is an effectiveness review required?

At least every two years. FINTRAC requires every reporting entity to review the effectiveness of its compliance program, covering its policies and procedures, risk assessment and training program, at a minimum once every two years. The review looks at how the program runs day to day as well as what the documents say.

### Who can carry out the review

FINTRAC's guidance says the review is carried out by an internal or external auditor or, if the business has no auditor, by the business itself. Whoever does it should know the requirements of the PCMLTFA and its regulations. An external review gives you independence and a fresh view.

### What a review tests

- whether your policies and procedures reflect current requirements and your current business;

- whether your risk assessment covers your clients, products, channels and geography, including sanctions evasion risk, and whether your controls follow from it;

- whether training happened, reached the right people and matches your risks;

- samples of client files, monitoring and reports to FINTRAC, to see how the program runs.

### Effectiveness review or FINTRAC examination?

An effectiveness review is your own check of your program. A FINTRAC examination is FINTRAC's assessment of your compliance. A recent, honest review, with its findings being fixed, is one of the best ways to prepare for an examination.

### Questions

**How often is an AML effectiveness review required in Canada?** At least every two years, covering your policies and procedures, risk assessment and training program.

**Can we do the review ourselves?** FINTRAC's guidance allows a self-review if you have no internal or external auditor, provided whoever does it knows the requirements. An external review adds independence.

**What do we receive?** Written findings and recommendations, in order of priority, so you know what to fix first.

**FINTRAC has contacted us about an examination. Where do we start?** Book a consultation. We review your program and records with you and help you prepare to show how it works.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Compliance program requirements](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/compliance-conformite/Guide4/4-eng). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Training

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/training.html

Anti-money laundering training for front-line staff, compliance teams and senior management.

**Fee:** Scoped (quoted after your consultation). Depends on the number of people, roles and sessions.

**Included:**
- Training built around your business
- Training for each role: front line, compliance and management
- A written training program and plan
- Training records

### Is AML training required in Canada?

Yes, if you have employees, agents or others authorized to act on your behalf. In that case a written, ongoing compliance training program, with a plan for delivering it, is one of the required elements of a compliance program for businesses regulated by FINTRAC. Training should fit your business and your risks, and reach the people who deal with clients or transactions. A sole proprietor with no employees, agents or others authorized to act for them doesn't need a training program.

### Training for each role

Front-line staff learn to recognize unusual activity, identify clients and know when and how to escalate. Compliance teams cover reviews, reporting, the 24-hour rule and deadlines, and how to document decisions. Senior management covers their responsibilities for the program and how to oversee it.

### Training records

Being able to show who was trained, on what and when is part of showing your program works. We help you keep those records, ready for your effectiveness review or a FINTRAC examination.

### Questions

**Is AML training mandatory in Canada?** Yes, if you have employees, agents or others authorized to act for you. A sole proprietor with no employees, agents or others acting for them doesn't need a training program.

**Who needs AML training?** Anyone whose work touches your compliance obligations, typically front-line staff, agents, compliance teams and senior management.

**Do you provide training records?** Yes. We help you keep records of who was trained, on what and when.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Compliance program requirements](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/compliance-conformite/Guide4/4-eng). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Company incorporation

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/incorporation-canada.html

Federal or Ontario incorporation, usually done within 24 hours. Fixed fee US$1,500.

**Fee:** US$1,500 (fixed fee · plus government filing fees). Government filing fees are separate: currently CA$200 federally online (CA$100 more for 4-hour express service) or CA$300 online in Ontario. A named Ontario company also needs an Ontario-biased Nuans name search report.

**Included:**
- Advice on federal or provincial incorporation
- Company name or numbered company
- Articles of incorporation filed
- Registered office address and first directors
- Set up ready for FINTRAC or RPAA registration
- Usually complete within 24 hours

### Federal or provincial?

You can incorporate federally, under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) through Corporations Canada, or in a province or territory, such as Ontario under its Business Corporations Act. A federal company can use its name across Canada, though it still registers in the provinces where it does business. A provincial company is often simpler if you'll operate mainly in one province. We help you choose before anything is filed.

### Directors and residency

Federal corporations must have at least 25% resident Canadian directors; if the company has fewer than four directors, at least one must be a resident Canadian. Under CBCA s.2, a resident Canadian includes a Canadian citizen ordinarily resident in Canada and a permanent resident ordinarily resident in Canada, with limited exceptions. Ontario doesn't require resident Canadian directors, which can matter for founders based outside Canada. Some regulated sectors have stricter rules.

### How long it takes

Once we have your details and documents, incorporation usually takes a few hours and is usually done within 24 hours; it isn't guaranteed. Corporations Canada processes online incorporations in about a day, with a 4-hour express option for an extra government fee, and Ontario incorporates immediately online.

### What it costs

Our fee is a fixed US$1,500. Government fees are paid separately to the government: currently CA$200 for federal online incorporation (CA$100 more for 4-hour express) or CA$300 for Ontario online incorporation.

For a federal online incorporation, the name search is built into the application, so a word name doesn't need a separate Nuans report. A named Ontario company needs an Ontario-biased Nuans name search report; a numbered company doesn't.

### After incorporation

- Keep corporate records, including a register of individuals with significant control.

- For a federal corporation, file information about individuals with significant control with Corporations Canada at incorporation, every year with the annual return, and within 15 days of a change to the register. This has applied since January 22, 2024.

- File an annual return each year (federal online annual return: CA$12).

- Register for tax accounts, and in each province where you carry on business.

- Register with [FINTRAC as an MSB](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration.html) or with the [Bank of Canada under the RPAA](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration.html) before you start offering those services.

### Questions

**How much does it cost to incorporate a company in Canada?** Our fee is a fixed US$1,500. Government filing fees are separate: currently CA$200 federally online or CA$300 in Ontario online.

**How long does incorporation take?** Usually within 24 hours once we have your details and documents, often a few hours. It isn't guaranteed.

**Can a non-resident incorporate in Canada?** Yes. Federal companies need at least 25% resident Canadian directors (at least one if there are fewer than four). Ontario doesn't require resident Canadian directors.

**Should we incorporate before registering as an MSB?** Usually, yes. The company is what registers with FINTRAC, so incorporating first means the registration can start straight away.

Sources: [Corporations Canada, Services, fees and processing times](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en/services-fees-and-processing-times); [Directors and officers](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en/business-corporations/directors-and-officers); [Next steps after incorporating](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en/business-corporations/next-steps-following-incorporation-your-business); [Individuals with significant control: file your information](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en/individuals-significant-control/individuals-significant-control-file-your-information); [Naming a corporation](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en/naming-corporation/naming-corporation-how-get-name); [Canada Business Corporations Act](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-44/); [Ontario, Register your business online](https://www.ontario.ca/page/business/start/register-your-business-online); [Ontario fees and timing](https://www.ontario.ca/page/cost-time-required-to-register-change-search-for-business-name-corporation-not-for-profit). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Guide: How to register an MSB in Canada

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/how-to-register-msb-canada.html

A money services business must register with FINTRAC before it starts operating, and renew every two years. FINTRAC doesn't charge a fee, and it says the majority of complete applications are processed within three months.

**Key points:**
- Register with FINTRAC before you start operating. FINTRAC doesn't charge a fee.
- Criminal record checks are needed for the CEO, president, directors and 20%+ owners.
- Answer FINTRAC's clarification requests within 30 days.
- Registration lasts two years. Report changes within 30 days.

### Step 1: Check whether you need to register

In Canada, a money services business (MSB) is a business that provides certain money services. If you have a place of business in Canada and you provide any of these, you must register with FINTRAC, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada, before you start:

- foreign exchange dealing;

- remitting or transmitting funds;

- issuing or redeeming money orders, traveller's cheques or similar negotiable instruments;

- dealing in virtual currency;

- crowdfunding platform services;

- armoured car services;

- cheque cashing;

- acquirer services for private automated banking machines.

If you have no place of business in Canada but you direct and provide these services to people or entities in Canada, you're a foreign MSB, and you must register too. Our [foreign MSB guide](https://amlcanada.ca/foreign-msb-registration-canada.html) covers that case.

Registering or being licensed with a province doesn't replace FINTRAC registration. Quebec has its own licence for money-services businesses, issued by Revenu Québec, which is needed in addition to FINTRAC registration.

If your business holds funds for users or transfers funds electronically for them, check the Retail Payment Activities Act as well. Many payment businesses need to register with the Bank of Canada as payment service providers, separately from FINTRAC. Our [RPAA guide](https://amlcanada.ca/rpaa-registration-guide.html) explains who is covered.

### Step 2: Gather what FINTRAC asks for

FINTRAC's registration asks for:

- details of the business, including its [incorporation](https://amlcanada.ca/incorporation-canada.html), ownership and senior management;

- bank account information;

- your compliance officer;

- how many employees you have, and every location you operate from;

- estimated annual transaction totals for each money service you offer;

- any agents or mandataries that provide services on your behalf;

- for a foreign MSB, a representative for service who lives in Canada;

- documents confirming the business exists and how it's owned and controlled;

- criminal record checks.

If you use agents or mandataries, you must also check that they're eligible before you engage them, including reviewing their criminal record checks. This has applied since October 1, 2025. For agents engaged before that date, MSBs have until October 1, 2027, according to [FINTRAC](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/msb-eng).

### Step 3: Order criminal record checks early

FINTRAC needs criminal record checks for the chief executive officer, the president, the directors, and anyone who owns or controls 20% or more of the business, directly or indirectly. A sole proprietor provides one for themselves.

Each check must come from a competent authority in the person's country of residence and be issued no more than six months before you apply. If a check isn't in English or French, it needs a translation attested by a certified translator, as [FINTRAC's registration page](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng) sets out. When owners and directors live in different countries, this is often the step that takes longest, so start it first.

### Step 4: Submit and answer FINTRAC's questions

Once everything is gathered and checked, you submit your registration to FINTRAC. FINTRAC may send clarification requests before it decides. You have 30 days to answer each one, and if you don't, FINTRAC may deny the application ([PCMLTFA section 11.14](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/P-24.501/FullText.html)). Once you're registered, the same 30-day rule applies, and FINTRAC may revoke a registration if a request goes unanswered.

Complete, consistent information is the best way to avoid back-and-forth. The transaction estimates, locations, ownership and documents should all tell the same story.

[FINTRAC says](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng) the majority of complete applications are processed within three months, and more complex ones can take longer. In our experience it has ranged from about a week to seven months, depending mostly on how complete the application is and on FINTRAC's workload. Our [MSB registration service](https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration.html) covers preparing and submitting the application.

### Step 5: Have your compliance program ready

Registration allows you to operate. Your obligations under the law start at the same time. From the day you start, you need a compliance program with five elements: a compliance officer, written policies and procedures, a risk assessment, an ongoing training program, and an effectiveness review at least every two years. You also need to identify clients, keep records, generally for at least five years, and report to FINTRAC.

It helps to build the program while the registration is in progress, so it's in place when you're registered. Our [compliance program documents](https://amlcanada.ca/compliance-programs.html) are written for this.

### Step 6: Stay registered

MSB registration is valid for two years and must be renewed before it expires. Between renewals, tell FINTRAC within 30 days when your registration information changes: a new address, new owners or directors, a new compliance officer, or a change in the services you offer. FINTRAC explains how on its [update and renewal page](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/respond-eng).

### Questions

**Does FINTRAC charge to register an MSB?** No. FINTRAC doesn't charge a registration fee. Your costs are your own time, criminal record checks, any certified translations, and professional help if you use it.

**Is there an MSB licence in Canada?** At the federal level, Canada requires registration with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. When people search for an MSB licence in Canada, they usually mean FINTRAC registration. Quebec is the exception: Revenu Québec issues a separate licence for money-services businesses.

**Can I register an MSB without a Canadian office?** Yes, as a foreign MSB, if you direct and provide money services to people in Canada. You'll need a representative for service who lives in Canada.

**Do I need a compliance program before registering?** You need it in place to operate, and FINTRAC asks for your compliance officer when you register. It makes sense to build both together.

**How long is MSB registration valid?** Two years. Changes to your registration information must be reported within 30 days.

**How long does FINTRAC take to approve an MSB registration?** FINTRAC says the majority of complete applications are processed within three months. In our experience it has ranged from about a week to seven months.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Register your MSB or FMSB](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng); [Money services businesses](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/msb-eng); [Update, renew or cancel your registration](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/respond-eng); [Compliance program requirements](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/compliance-conformite/Guide4/4-eng); [Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/P-24.501/FullText.html); [Revenu Québec, Money-services business licence](https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/sector-specific-measures/money-services-businesses-msbs/money-services-business-licence-application/). Checked 11 October 2026.

## Guide: How much does MSB registration cost in Canada?

URL: https://amlcanada.ca/msb-registration-cost-canada.html

FINTRAC doesn't charge a fee to register a money services business. The costs come from criminal record checks, translations, documents and the compliance program you need to operate.

**Key points:**
- FINTRAC registration itself is free.
- Budget for criminal record checks, certified translations and documents.
- You need a compliance program in place before you operate.
- Our fixed fees: US$3,500 registration; US$3,500 program documents.

### FINTRAC's fee: none

[FINTRAC](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng) doesn't charge a fee to register a money services business, or to renew. If anyone tells you there's a government fee for FINTRAC MSB registration, ask what it's for.

### The other costs of registering

Criminal record checks are one of the main outside costs. FINTRAC needs one for the CEO, the president, each director and anyone owning or controlling 20% or more, and each must be issued within six months before you apply. Costs vary by country and by provider.

Any check or document that isn't in English or French needs a translation attested by a certified translator. You'll also need corporate documents showing the business exists and how it's owned and controlled.

If you don't have a Canadian company yet, there are government incorporation fees, currently CA$200 federally online or CA$300 in Ontario online. Where provincial licensing applies, there are fees for that too: Quebec licenses money-services businesses separately through [Revenu Québec](https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/sector-specific-measures/money-services-businesses-msbs/money-services-business-licence-application/), which sets its own fees.

Then there's time: gathering and checking everything, and answering FINTRAC's clarification requests within 30 days. Our [step-by-step registration guide](https://amlcanada.ca/how-to-register-msb-canada.html) shows where the time goes.

### What it costs to operate once registered

To operate, an MSB needs a compliance program: a compliance officer, policies and procedures, a risk assessment, training and an effectiveness review at least every two years. It also has to report to FINTRAC and keep records. These are ongoing costs, whether you staff them in-house or outsource them. Our [compliance program documents](https://amlcanada.ca/compliance-programs.html) cover the written part at a fixed fee.

### What professional help costs with us

| Service | Fee |

| Canadian company incorporation | US$1,500, fixed (government fees separate) |

| FINTRAC MSB registration | US$3,500, fixed |

| PCMLTFA compliance program (14 documents) | US$3,500, fixed |

| Outsourced compliance officer | US$1,500 per 10 hours |

| Canadian business address | US$200 per month |

| Registered MSB to acquire | From €28,000 |

All fees are on our [pricing page](https://amlcanada.ca/pricing.html). Every engagement starts with a consultation and a written scope, so you know the fee before any work begins.

### Registering vs buying a registered MSB

Some businesses buy a company that's already registered instead of registering a new one. It costs more up front. It still needs due diligence, updates to FINTRAC within 30 days of changes like new owners and directors, criminal record checks for the new people, and a compliance program that fits the new owners. Our guide to [buying an MSB](https://amlcanada.ca/buying-an-msb-canada.html) covers what to check.

### Questions

**Is FINTRAC MSB registration free?** Yes. FINTRAC doesn't charge to register or renew.

**How much does it cost to set up an MSB in Canada?** Registration is free, but budget for criminal record checks, certified translations, documents and a compliance program. Our fixed fees are US$3,500 for registration and US$3,500 for compliance program documents.

**Does Quebec charge for an MSB licence?** Yes. Quebec licenses money-services businesses separately through Revenu Québec, which sets its own fees.

Sources: [FINTRAC, Register your MSB or FMSB](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/reg-ins-eng); [Update, renew or cancel your registration](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/msb-esm/register-inscrire/respond-eng); [Compliance program requirements](https://fintrac-canafe.canada.ca/guidance-directives/compliance-conformite/Guide4/4-eng); [Revenu Québec, Money-services business licence](https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/sector-specific-measures/money-services-businesses-msbs/money-services-business-licence-application/).
